glossary.prostate: A gland below the male bladder around the urethra; enlargement can block urine flow.
glossary.neurological disease: Disease of the brain, spinal cord or nerves, such as stroke, MS or Parkinson's.
glossary.menopause: The end of periods; falling oestrogen weakens pelvic tissues.
glossary.cognitive impairment: Reduced memory and thinking, as in dementia.
glossary.frequency: Needing to pass urine more often than normal.
glossary.urgency: A sudden compelling need to pass urine that is hard to put off.
glossary.poor stream: A weak flow of urine, often from outlet obstruction such as BPH.
glossary.incomplete emptying: The feeling that the bladder is not empty after voiding.
glossary.exertion: Physical effort, such as lifting or exercise.
glossary.intra-abdominal pressure: Pressure inside the abdomen, raised by coughing, sneezing, lifting or obesity.
glossary.sphincter: A ring of muscle that closes an opening, here the urethra.
glossary.prolapse: Pelvic organs such as the bladder or uterus dropping into the vagina from weak support.
glossary.caffeine: A stimulant in coffee and tea that irritates the bladder and increases urine output.
glossary.chronic urinary retention: Long-term failure to empty the bladder fully, often painless.
glossary.urethral obstruction: A blockage of the urethra, such as a stricture or enlarged prostate.
glossary.neuropathy: Damage to nerves, for example from diabetes, impairing bladder control.
glossary.spinal cord disease: Damage to the spinal cord, disrupting nerve control of the bladder.
glossary.anticholinergics: Drugs that block acetylcholine; they relax the bladder and can cause retention.
glossary.Parkinson's: A progressive brain disease with tremor, stiffness and slow movement; can cause bladder dysfunction.
glossary.dribbling: Slow, uncontrolled leaking of small amounts of urine.
glossary.distended bladder: An overfilled, stretched bladder, often palpable above the pubic bone.
glossary.dementia: Progressive decline in memory and thinking.
glossary.delirium: An acute, fluctuating confusional state, often triggered by illness or drugs.
glossary.frailty: Reduced physical reserve in older people, raising risk of falls and disability.
glossary.mobility: The ability to move around, such as walking to the toilet.
glossary.differential: Another diagnosis that could explain the same features.
glossary.urinary dye studies: Tests putting coloured dye in the bladder to see whether it leaks into the vagina.
glossary.back pain: Pain in the back; with new retention it may signal cauda equina compression.
glossary.urinalysis: Testing urine for blood, protein, glucose, leucocytes and nitrites.
glossary.urine dipstick: A strip dipped in urine that changes colour to show blood, glucose or infection.
glossary.bladder scan: A bedside ultrasound measuring how much urine is in the bladder.
glossary.postural hypotension: A fall in blood pressure on standing, causing dizziness and falls.
glossary.glaucoma: Raised pressure in the eye that damages the optic nerve; anticholinergics can trigger angle closure.
glossary.constipation: Infrequent or hard stools; straining worsens pelvic floor weakness.
glossary.beta-3 agonist: A drug that stimulates beta-3 receptors in the bladder wall, relaxing the detrusor.
glossary.myasthenia gravis: An autoimmune disease blocking nerve-muscle signals, causing fatigable weakness.
glossary.catheterisation: Passing a tube into the bladder to drain urine.
glossary.acute retention: Sudden, painful inability to pass urine.
glossary.urethral sphincter: The muscle ring around the urethra that keeps urine in.
glossary.filling phase: The part of the bladder cycle when it is filling and should stay relaxed.
glossary.cortical inhibition: The brain's conscious suppression of bladder contraction until it is convenient.
glossary.outlet obstruction: Blockage at the bladder neck or urethra, such as from BPH.
glossary.atonic: Lacking muscle tone, so it cannot contract properly.
glossary.anticholinergic side effects: Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, retention and confusion from blocking acetylcholine.
glossary.lower urinary tract: The bladder and urethra (and prostate in men).
glossary.toileting: Getting to and using the toilet.
